name: QuNeo
summary: Single-port family. Older firmware used QUNEO in all caps; newer firmware uses QuNeo. Bootloader is indicated by PID MSB = 1.

notes: QuNeo's identity reply encodes its version in only two bytes, not the standard three: the MSB nibble-packed as (major<<4)|minor, the LSB the patch. The standard parse misreads this layout and reports an inflated major version (e.g. a healthy 1.2.31 misread as 18.0.0) even though the device is fine; versionEncoding bcd16 unpacks it correctly.

chunkDelayMs is pure inter-chunk pacing, independent of the reply-wait budget (see idReplyTimeoutMs/idReplyResendAttempts) - set explicitly here at the same value as the CLI default only to document that it's intentional, not an oversight.

The bootloader has a firmware bug: it can flush its own USB IN FIFO and discard an already-queued identity-reply packet, losing the reply outright rather than sending it late. A short per-attempt timeout is cheap since a lost reply never arrives no matter how long you wait; a high resend count is what actually recovers the transfer, since each resend is an independent chance to avoid the race. Do not copy these values to other families without their own evidence they need it.
The bootloader erases its whole application region when it recognizes the first firmware packet, blocking USB until that finishes, so chunk 1's reply needs extra grace beyond the steady-state delay.
QuNeo reboots straight into application mode as it commits the final chunk and never answers an identity request on the bootloader port afterwards.
Requests a reboot into bootloader mode for QuNeo devices.
Single unchunked payload, superseded by firmware_1_2_31_chunked's chunk-safe packaging.
Chunk-safe (-cs128) packaging via the shared Hex_to_SysEx tool.
Superseded by firmware_1_2_31_chunked_cs512 - this cs128 packaging's much larger chunk count made it far more likely to hit the bootloader's identity-reply race (see firmwareUpdateDefaults notes).
Chunk-safe (-cs512) repackaging of the same v1.2.31 image with a larger chunk-safe window (321 chunks vs the cs128 packaging's 1164), reducing exposure to the bootloader's identity-reply race.
